html:
Tibeto-Burmanese is the map's label, around 2000 BCE, for the early peoples of the Tibetan Plateau and its edges, speakers of languages of the Sino-Tibetan family, the family of Chinese, Tibetan and Burmese.

Farmers from the upper Yellow River, linked to cultures such as Majiayao, moved onto the eastern and southern edges of the plateau from about 3000 BCE, growing millet in the lower valleys. Later, around 1600 BCE, barley and sheep let people settle year round at heights above 3,000 metres. Hunters had used the plateau long before.

These groups are among the ancestors of the Tibetans and many peoples of the Himalaya and Burma. See also the proto-Tibetan cultures, and the later Zhangzhung kingdom.
sum: Tibeto-Burmanese is the map's label, around 2000 BCE, for the early peoples of the Tibetan Plateau and its edges, speakers of languages of the Sino-Tibetan family, the family of Chinese, Tibetan and Burmese.
